incident_report.incident: Shortly after the start was eased when crowded between ZOUPER FELLOW and LEAN MASTER which shifted out slightly.  Sent for sampling post-race.
C L Chau was reprimanded for using his whip in a manner where the hand holding the whip was above shoulder height on one occasion near the 100 Metres.  Sent for sampling post-race.
No report.

Shifted in at the start and was bumped.  Prior to declaring weighed-in the Stewards viewed the patrol films to ascertain if there were grounds for a protest/objection on behalf of the 4th placegetter SUPER SIXTY after being steadied at the 150 Metres.  When the Stewards were satisfied SUPER SIXTY had not established clear running between BEAUTY THUNDER and ZETA HEDGE they declined a protest/objection.  When questioned H Bowman stated that after following ZETA HEDGE into the Home Straight he observed that runner lay out on straightening and therefore he elected to endeavour to improve between ZETA HEDGE and BEAUTY THUNDER.  He said when ZETA HEDGE then shifted in at the 250 Metres SUPER SIXTY was held up for clear running between the 250 Metres and the 150 Metres and when BEAUTY THUNDER shifted out slightly he was obliged to steady his mount at the 150 Metres.  C L Chau, rider of ZETA HEDGE, was advised to exercise more care.  Sent for sampling post-race.
From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.
In the middle stages raced keenly when being shifted behind SUPER SIXTY to obtain cover.
Jumped awkwardly.
Making the first turn leaving the 600 Metres shifted out when positioned close to HAPPY BOYS.

M L Yeung reported that he was instructed to take up a forward position.  He said when unable to cross runners to his inside GOLDEN FRIENDSHIP was obliged to race wide and without cover before giving ground in the Home Straight.  Trainer K H Ting confirmed the instructions issued.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
Jumped only fairly.  Making the first turn near the 600 Metres became unbalanced when racing tight to the inside of BEAUTY THUNDER.
Jumped awkwardly and shortly after the start raced in restricted room between BEAUTY THUNDER and SUPER SIXTY.
No report.

Withdrawn on 20.10.25 by order of the Stewards acting on veterinary advice (left front tendon injury) and replaced by Standby Declared Starter WARRIORS DREAM.  Before being allowed to race again, FIELD MARSHAL will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.

C L Chau was severely reprimanded for using his whip in a manner where the hand holding the whip was above shoulder height on one occasion near the 100 Metres.

Jumped awkwardly and became unbalanced.  Y L Chung stated that his intention was to hold a more forward position but after being crowded at the start his mount settled back in the field.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.
No report.

Shortly after the start was bumped by NOBLE DELUXE which shifted in.  Apprentice E C W Wong stated that he was given the option of holding a more forward position.  He said when GLORY CLOUD jumped well he elected to allow the horse to stride forward and race outside the lead.
On jumping was bumped by RUN RUN TIMING which shifted out.
Shortly after the start was bumped by GLORY CLOUD which shifted in.  Leaving the 300 Metres M L Yeung dropped his left side rein for a short distance.
Shifted in at the start and was bumped.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.

Shortly after the start was bumped by WISDOM STAR which shifted in and away from GLORY CLOUD after bumping with that runner.  Near the 450 Metres was bumped by PODIUM which shifted to the outside of HAPPY HORSE.  Near the 400 Metres was eased and shifted to the outside of CAMP FIRE to obtain clear running.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

After travelling a short distance was eased when crowded between WOODFIRE CHAMP and COLONEL which shifted out.  K C Leung (WOODFIRE CHAMP) pleaded guilty to a charge of careless riding [Rule 100(1)] in that approaching the first turn near the 1000 Metres he allowed his mount to shift in when not clear of CAMP FIRE, resulting in CAMP FIRE having to be checked to avoid WOODFIRE CHAMP.  K C Leung was suspended from riding in races for one Hong Kong raceday to be conducted on Thursday, 30 October 2025 at Sha Tin.  In assessing penalty, the Stewards determined the carelessness grade 2 and the consequences grade 2 and also considered his excellent race riding record.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

K C Leung pleaded guilty to a careless riding charge for causing interference approaching the first turn near the 1000 Metres (see CAMP FIRE).  K C Leung could offer no explanation for his mount’s disappointing performance.  Trainer C W Chang advised the horse had pleased him leading into the race and expected it to perform well.  He could offer no excuse for its disappointing performance.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of WOODFIRE CHAMP was considered disappointing as compared to its previous race starts.  Before being allowed to race again, WOODFIRE CHAMP will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
L Hewitson stated that he was asked to hold an on-pace position and after commencing well he was able to comply with the instructions  issued.  Sent for sampling post-race.

Shifted in at the start and made contact with ISLAND BREEZES when being corrected by its rider.  Approaching the 200 Metres made contact with HAPPY PARK due to both runners shifting ground.  Raced wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Sent for sampling post-race.

After the event the Veterinary Surgeon reported that WRITTEN CASA was lame in its left front leg.  Before being allowed to race again, WRITTEN CASA will be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
Sent for sampling post-race.

No report.

After being crossed by HAPPY PARK near the 1000 Metres commenced to race keenly and was steadied to avoid HAPPY PARK for some distance.  M F Poon stated that after jumping awkwardly his mount was unable to cross to the front and lead as instructed and this resulted in PATCH OF WATCH not finishing the race off in the Home Straight as PATCH OF WATCH races best when able to dictate in front.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

Bumped at the start.  Making the Home Turn was steadied and shifted to the outside of SUPER UNIVERSAL when it endeavoured to improve into a doubtful run between SUPER UNIVERSAL and SUPER PACE which shifted out.  Sent for sampling post-race.

When questioned L Hewitson stated that after entering the Home Straight he improved to the inside of SUPER PACE with a view to obtaining clear running inside NEBRASKAN.  He stated that as his mount commenced to improve NEBRASKAN shifted in which then resulted in STAR FIGURE being crowded for room between the 200 Metres and the 100 Metres and having to be steadied as a consequence.  As the Stewards were satisfied that STAR FIGURE had not established clear running to the inside of NEBRASKAN before NEBRASKAN commenced to shift in no action was taken.  Sent for sampling post-race.
Shifted out abruptly at the start and was bumped.  Sent for sampling post-race.

From the outside barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Raced keenly in the middle stages.  When questioned regarding his riding Apprentice E C W Wong stated that from the outside barrier he was instructed to ride his mount in a conservative manner in the early stages and endeavour to obtain runs to the inside in the Home Straight.  He said after settling back in the field his mount was positioned behind CALIFORNIA DEEPLY throughout the race and from the 500 Metres he elected to remain racing behind that runner to comply with his instructions to take inside runs.  He added that when VON BAER continued to travel well this resulted in it improving to the inside of CALIFORNIA DEEPLY and then being held up behind FLYING TING LOK in the Home Straight.  When questioned as to why he did not improve to the outside of CALIFORNIA DEEPLY Apprentice Wong stated that his focus was on complying with his instructions but in retrospect he agreed with the Stewards that his best option would have been to improve to the outside of CALIFORNIA DEEPLY after the 500 Metres.  Trainer D A Hayes confirmed the instructions issued and in particular confirmed he had requested Apprentice Wong to endeavour to take runs towards the inside in the Home Straight.  After considering his explanation and the instructions issued the Stewards found the tactics adopted by Apprentice Wong were reasonable in the circumstances.
On jumping became unbalanced when bumped by KING OBERON.

Jumped only fairly.  From a wide barrier was shifted across behind runners in the early stages.  Leaving the 300 Metres RISING PHOENIX commenced to improve to the inside of HAPPY BUDDIES (K C Leung).  A short distance later RISING PHOENIX was then shifted to the inside to obtain clear running before Jockey Leung corrected his mount.  As a consequence RISING PHOENIX was then checked when it was crowded by HAPPY BUDDIES.  K C Leung was severely reprimanded and advised in similar circumstances he would be expected to ensure that he is clear before shifting ground.  However, the Stewards were satisfied that he had endeavoured to straighten his mount just prior to shifting in into the running of RISING PHOENIX.  RISING PHOENIX was then shifted to the outside of HAPPY BUDDIES and SUPER PACE to obtain clear running near the 150 Metres.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

H Bowman stated that his instructions were to go forward from his wide barrier.  He said when unable to cross runners to his inside this resulted in DENFIELD being obliged to race wide and without cover for the majority of the event.  Trainer C S Shum confirmed the instructions and said he issued those instructions as he believed it was advantageous to race in a more forward position having regard to the track pattern tonight.  A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.

B Avdulla stated that his mount, which was having its first race start at Happy Valley, hung out throughout the event and failed to finish the race off in the Home Straight.  Trainer A S Cruz stated that he had expected the horse to perform well but concurred with the views offered by Jockey Avdulla that CALIFORNIA BAY may not have been suited racing at Happy Valley. A veterinary inspection immediately following the race did not show any significant findings.  The performance of CALIFORNIA BAY was considered disappointing.  Before being allowed to race again, CALIFORNIA BAY will be required to perform to the satisfaction of the Stewards in a barrier trial and be subjected to an official veterinary examination.
